title: Galois stability of the weight strata
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and let
$k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and an
algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. Put

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}
=\{z\in\Qlb:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}.
$$

For $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$, call
$\alpha$ a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$ when

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
\quad\text{for every }\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C;
$$

this is the Weil-number condition, and the
algebraic-closure convention fixes
the ell-adic comparison field. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically connected
of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
Fix indeterminates $T$ and $U$.
Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series.
Let $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfy

$$
Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T),\qquad A(0)=B(0)=1,\qquad
\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T],
$$

the normalized integral-fraction
conditions; fix such a normalized presentation. For
$C\in\{A,B\}$, let
$r=\deg C$ and define its reciprocal polynomial

$$
C^\#(U)=U^rC(U^{-1})
$$

Its roots, with multiplicity, are the reciprocal roots in the
reciprocal-root convention;
their inverses are the corresponding ordinary roots. For every integer $i$ with
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
R_i=
\begin{cases}
\text{the submultiset of roots of \(A^\#\) that are \(q\)-Weil numbers
of weight \(i\)},& i\text{ odd},\\
\text{the submultiset of roots of \(B^\#\) that are \(q\)-Weil numbers
of weight \(i\)},& i\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

Assume that every reciprocal root occurring in $A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has a
unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and that the displayed $q$-Weil
condition is invariant under every embedding of its number field into
$\mathbf C$. Then for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ each
$R_i$ is stable, with multiplicities, under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.

proof.text: Fix $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ and $\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$. Set $C=A$ if $i$ is odd and $C=B$ if $i$ is even. Write $C(T)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jT^j$, where $c_0=1$ and $c_r\neq0$. By the polynomial-ring and coefficient-map definitions, $f(U):=C^\#(U)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jU^{r-j}$ has rational (indeed integer) coefficients. It is monic, and $f(0)=c_r\neq0$. Regard it in $\overline{\mathbf Q}[U]$. Applying $\gamma$ to its coefficients leaves $f$ unchanged, since $\gamma$ fixes $\mathbf Q$. This also covers $r=0$, when $C=f=1$.

source.place: ## Proof, first clause: rational coefficients of A^#, B^#

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-injective-map] with $K=L=\overline{\mathbf Q}$, $P=f$, and the injective ring homomorphism $\gamma$. The coefficientwise image of $f$ is $f$ by Step 1, so for every $x\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ we obtain $m_x(f)=m_{\gamma(x)}(f)$. By [def-weil-root-multiplicity], these are the multiplicities of $x$ and $\gamma(x)$ in the root multiset of the nonzero polynomial $f$. In particular roots are carried to roots with exactly the same multiplicity, and $\gamma^{-1}$ provides the inverse permutation.

source.place: ## Proof, first clause and final phrase: root multisets are stable, with multiplicities

proof.text: Let $W_i(x)$ mean that $x\neq0$ is a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$ as in [def-weil-numbers], and set $W_i(0)$ to false. The last assertion of [lem-embedding-extension] gives $W_i(x)\Rightarrow W_i(\gamma(x))$. It applies to the same finite-field datum and algebraic closure as here. Concretely, for each embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\gamma(x))\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, the restriction of $\gamma$ maps $\mathbf Q(x)$ isomorphically to $\mathbf Q(\gamma(x))$, so $\tau\circ\gamma$ is an embedding and $|\tau(\gamma(x))|=q^{i/2}$. Apply the same stability assertion with $\gamma^{-1}$ to obtain the converse. Thus $W_i(\gamma(x))\Longleftrightarrow W_i(x)$; for $x=0$ both predicates are false.

source.place: ## Proof, second clause: the Weil condition is Galois-stable

proof.text: By the definition of the submultiset $R_i$, the number of copies of $x$ in $R_i$ is $m_x(f)$ when $W_i(x)$ holds, and is $0$ otherwise. Steps 2 and 3 therefore give the same number of copies for $x$ and $\gamma(x)$. Since $\gamma$ is a bijection, the number of copies of any $y$ in the image multiset $\gamma(R_i)$ is the number of copies of $\gamma^{-1}(y)$ in $R_i$, which equals the number of copies of $y$ in $R_i$. Hence $\gamma(R_i)=R_i$ with multiplicities. This holds for either parity of $i$, every allowed $i$, and every $\gamma$, proving the assertion.

source.place: ## Proof, final sentence: the weight submultiset is stable with multiplicities
